mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of over 10% in the same month predicts a contractionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of 0.4 percentage points or more over the prior month during a period when payroll employment (PAYEMS) is flat or declining indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises >= 0.4pp AND PAYEMS <= previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically distinguishable from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a persistent supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month for 3 consecutive months AND monthly change <= -0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a period of negative core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY < 0%) signals an emergency easing, which boosts risk asset valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% alongside a concurrent decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (proxied by GDPC1 monthly change) signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a softening economic cycle and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 5% AND GDPC1 monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of 0.2 percentage points or more for four consecutive months, regardless of regime, predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to persistent labor market weakness.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline of at least 1% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based supply contraction, which raises costs and reduces demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change <= -1% AND HOUST monthly change <= -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero.
